Data is stored with a 0.1 mm precision." Empirical support: pooled hourly r vs Stage IV hour-ending stamps on 2014-01-02 peaks at lag 0 (0.515) vs 0.453 (-1h) and 0.467 (+1h) - weak but consistent.
open_meteo_era5.multi_point: Yes: &latitude=52.52,48.85&longitude=13.41,2.35 (docs). Tested: 12 centroids in one call -> HTTP 200, JSON list of 12, 23999 B; era5 snaps to 0.25 deg grid (e.g. 36.4,-79.197 -> 36.5,-79.25).
open_meteo_era5.free_tier: non-commercial, no key: < 10,000 calls/day, 5,000/hour, 600/min (terms page); pricing page: 300,000 calls/month; a request with > 10 variables or > 2 weeks for one location counts as several calls (fractional counting: 2 weeks x 15 variables = 1.5 calls, 4 weeks = 3.0).
open_meteo_era5.note: model reanalysis rain, not observed; already cached by project

without_account.product: NOAA AORC v1.1 hourly 1 km (AWS Zarr)
without_account.why: 1980-2014 fully covered, hour-ending UTC stamps, ~1.8 GB for 12 basins 2000-2014 (est.), reproduces Stage IV hourly (r=0.99 on test), one script, no extra libraries
without_account.caveats: retrospective analysis (not real-time; ~10 day lag); pre-2002 hours are disaggregated daily gauge totals

without_account.product: NCEP Stage IV hourly via IEM mirror (2002-2014; ST4 files exist from 2000)
without_account.why: the real-time radar+gauge product; ~1 h latency in operation; GDAL GRIB read works in project venv
without_account.caveats: ~128 GB, ~30 h of crawling at 6-way (est.); volunteer server; 2002+ only

without_account.product: IMERG V07 Late/Early half-hourly via dynamical.org Icechunk (AWS)
without_account.why: the satellite rain asked for; 1998-present; ~0.4-0.7 GB (est.); Early ~5 h / Late ~15 h lag
without_account.caveats: needs Python>=3.12 + icechunk>=2; time-stamp semantics unresolved; large single-event errors; Final run not available
184 GB, slow server (118 KB/s), satellite-only: not worth it
